mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 0.1% relative to its 12-month moving average signals active monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in FEDFUNDS < 0.1% periods show no significant positive skew (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 5.0% triggers negative equity returns due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings growth in the subsequent 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in UNRATE > 5.0% periods show no significant negative skew (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) below their 6-month moving averages indicate weakening consumer demand, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in HOUST/INDPRO < 6mo_avg periods show no significant negative skew (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 100 (index 2017=100) signals manufacturing slowdown, reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in INDPRO < 100 during late-cycle expansion show no significant negative skew (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increase above 235.0 (index 1982-1984=100) signals inflationary pressure prompting monetary tightening, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in CPIAUCSL > 235.0 periods show no significant negative skew (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below its 12-month moving average indicates labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth to produce negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in PAYEMS < 12mo_avg periods show no significant negative skew (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In post-shock recovery regimes, housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1000.0 (thousands of units) signals strengthening consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in HOUST > 1000.0 during post-shock recovery show no significant positive skew (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average indicates supply chain disruption, reducing corporate output and profit margins to produce negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in INDPRO < 6mo_avg periods show no significant negative skew (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
